claim: GABAergic fast-spiking parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons are frequently myelinated in the cerebral cortex.
source: GABAergic fast-spiking parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons are frequently myelinated in the cerebral cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work (Micheva et al., 2016; Stedehouder et al., 2017) in the introduction.

claim: Segmental myelination along neocortical interneuron axons is strongly predicted by the joint combination of interbranch distance and local axon caliber.
source: Here, we report that segmental myelination along neocortical interneuron axons is strongly predicted by the joint combination of interbranch distance and local axon caliber.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ROC analysis data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Enlargement of PV+ interneurons increased axonal myelination.
source: Enlargement of PV+ interneurons increased axonal myelination, while reduced cell size led to decreased myelination.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data from PV::TSC1 mice shown in Figure 5.

claim: Reduced PV+ interneuron cell size led to decreased myelination.
source: Enlargement of PV+ interneurons increased axonal myelination, while reduced cell size led to decreased myelination.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data from PV::UBE3A mice shown in Figure 5.

claim: Regular-spiking SOM+ cells normally have relatively shorter interbranch distances and thinner axon diameters than PV+ cells.
source: Next, we considered regular-spiking SOM+ cells, which normally have relatively shorter interbranch distances and thinner axon diameters than PV+ cells, and are rarely myelinated.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by morphological measurements shown in Figure 6.

claim: SOM+ cells are rarely myelinated.
source: Next, we considered regular-spiking SOM+ cells, which normally have relatively shorter interbranch distances and thinner axon diameters than PV+ cells, and are rarely myelinated.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6 showing only 1 of 10 SOM+ cells was myelinated.

claim: Enlargement of SOM+ cell size dramatically increased the frequency of myelinated axonal segments.
source: Consistent with the importance of axonal morphology for guiding interneuron myelination, enlargement of SOM+ cell size dramatically increased the frequency of myelinated axonal segments.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data from SOM::TSC1 mice shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: The findings on interneuron axonal myelination extend to human neocortex.
source: Lastly, we confirm that these findings also extend to human neocortex by quantifying interneuron axonal myelination from ex vivo surgical tissue.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data from human tissue shown in Figure 9.

claim: A large fraction of neocortical myelination arises from axons of fast-spiking, parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons.
source: Recent studies have shown that a large fraction of neocortical myelination arises from axons of fast-spiking, parvalbumin-positive (PV) interneurons (Micheva et al., 2016; Stedehouder et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: Nearly every cortical PV+ interneuron is myelinated.
source: Nearly every cortical PV+ interneuron is myelinated, and most frequently with a proximally-biased axonal topography consisting of short internodes interspersed with branch points (Stedehouder et al., 2017; Stedehouder et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: PV+ interneuron myelination exhibits a proximally-biased axonal topography consisting of short internodes interspersed with branch points.
source: Nearly every cortical PV+ interneuron is myelinated, and most frequently with a proximally-biased axonal topography consisting of short internodes interspersed with branch points (Stedehouder et al., 2017; Stedehouder et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: Other neocortical GABAergic interneuron subtypes are more rarely and sparsely myelinated.
source: In contrast, other neocortical GABAergic interneuron subtypes are more rarely and sparsely myelinated, raising the question of what factors determine this cell type-restricted pattern of neocortical interneuron myelination.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In the peripheral nervous system (PNS), a critical threshold of axonal diameter of ~1 µm largely predicts myelination.
source: In the peripheral nervous system (PNS), a critical threshold of axonal diameter of ~1 µm has been identified, which largely predicts myelination (Duncan, 1934).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation to prior work.

claim: In the central nervous system (CNS), axons with diameters ~200 nm can become myelinated.
source: Axons with diameters ~200 nm can become myelinated (Hildebrand et al., 1993), while axon diameters as large as ~800 nm can remain unmyelinated (Hildebrand et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation to prior work.

claim: In the CNS, axon diameters as large as ~800 nm can remain unmyelinated.
source: Axons with diameters ~200 nm can become myelinated (Hildebrand et al., 1993), while axon diameters as large as ~800 nm can remain unmyelinated (Hildebrand et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation to prior work.

claim: In vitro, oligodendrocytes reliably initiate myelination of synthetic nanofibers above a critical diameter of ~300 nm.
source: In vitro, oligodendrocytes reliably initiate myelination of synthetic nanofibers above a critical diameter of ~300 nm but rarely do so for smaller diameters (Lee et al., 2012a; Bechler et al., 2015; Goebbels et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: Oligodendrocytes rarely initiate myelination of synthetic nanofibers below ~300 nm diameter.
source: In vitro, oligodendrocytes reliably initiate myelination of synthetic nanofibers above a critical diameter of ~300 nm but rarely do so for smaller diameters (Lee et al., 2012a; Bechler et al., 2015; Goebbels et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: In grey matter in vivo, myelinated axons <300 nm are rarely observed.
source: The diameter findings appear to extend to grey matter in vivo, where myelinated axons <300 nm are rarely observed (Micheva et al., 2016; Goebbels et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: Following acute demyelination, regenerated myelin sheaths often re-establish their pre-morbid pattern of myelination.
source: Moreover, following acute demyelination regenerated myelin sheaths often re-establish their pre-morbid pattern of myelination, suggesting that intrinsic axonal factors are primary determinants of myelination (Auer et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation to prior work.

claim: Intrinsic axonal factors are primary determinants of myelination.
source: Moreover, following acute demyelination regenerated myelin sheaths often re-establish their pre-morbid pattern of myelination, suggesting that intrinsic axonal factors are primary determinants of myelination (Auer et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from cited work.

claim: Oligodendrocytes sense axonal diameters in vitro and adjust their internode length based on fiber diameter.
source: Furthermore, oligodendrocytes appear to sense axonal diameters in vitro, and adjust their internode length based on fiber diameter (Bechler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation to prior work.

claim: Axonal diameter is only moderately predictive of myelination topography in the CNS.
source: However, in contrast to its high predictive validity in the PNS, axonal diameter is only moderately predictive of myelination topography in the CNS.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a summary of prior work.

claim: Recorded PV+ cells exhibited the fast-spiking pattern associated with PV+ interneurons.
source: Recorded cells exhibited the fast-spiking pattern associated with PV+ interneurons (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1c.

claim: PV+ interneuron axon shaft diameter averaged 0.34 ± 0.01 µm (range 0.16–0.98 µm).
source: Axon shaft diameter averaged 0.34 ± 0.01 µm (range 0.16–0.98 µm) and decreased with increasing branch order (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1.

claim: PV+ interneuron axon shaft diameter decreased with increasing branch order.
source: Axon shaft diameter averaged 0.34 ± 0.01 µm (range 0.16–0.98 µm) and decreased with increasing branch order (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1g.

claim: PV+ interneuron en passant boutons averaged 0.71 ± 0.01 µm in diameter (range 0.34–1.26 µm).
source: En passant boutons, located primarily on more distal branches (≥5th branch order), averaged 0.71 ± 0.01 µm in diameter (range 0.34–1.26 µm; Figure 1h).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1h.

claim: En passant boutons are located primarily on more distal branches (≥5th branch order) of PV+ interneurons.
source: En passant boutons, located primarily on more distal branches (≥5th branch order), averaged 0.71 ± 0.01 µm in diameter (range 0.34–1.26 µm; Figure 1h).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: Reconstructed PV+ interneurons consistently exhibited myelination of their proximal axons (8 out of 8; 100%).
source: Consistent with previous studies (Stedehouder et al., 2017; Stedehouder et al., 2018), reconstructed PV+ interneurons consistently exhibited myelination of their proximal axons (8 out of 8; 100%, Figure 2a,c), while distal axonal segments remained unmyelinated (Figure 2b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Distal axonal segments of PV+ interneurons remained unmyelinated.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Stedehouder et al., 2017; Stedehouder et al., 2018), reconstructed PV+ interneurons consistently exhibited myelination of their proximal axons (8 out of 8; 100%, Figure 2a,c), while distal axonal segments remained unmyelinated (Figure 2b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Myelination of PV+ interneurons typically extended from branch point to branch point.
source: Myelination of PV+ interneurons typically extended from branch point to branch point (Figure 2c), in which ~84% of myelinated internodes had their boundaries within 5 µm of an axonal branch point (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: ~84% of myelinated internodes had their boundaries within 5 µm of an axonal branch point.
source: Myelination of PV+ interneurons typically extended from branch point to branch point (Figure 2c), in which ~84% of myelinated internodes had their boundaries within 5 µm of an axonal branch point (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Axon shaft diameter strongly co-varied with myelination, with a critical univariate threshold at 334 nm (area under curve, AUC = 0.93; sensitivity = 97.2%, specificity = 84.4%).
source: Axon shaft diameter strongly co-varied with myelination, with a critical univariate threshold at 334 nm (area under curve, AUC = 0.93; sensitivity = 97.2%, specificity = 84.4%), above which internodes were often present and below which myelination was rarely observed (Figure 2e–g).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: 30% of interbranch segments with axon shaft diameter >334 nm remained incorrectly classified by the univariate ROC model (15 of 50 segments).
source: However, 30% of interbranch segments with axon shaft diameter >334 nm remained incorrectly classified by the univariate ROC model (15 of 50 segments), suggesting additional deterministic factors underlying the variance in segmental myelination.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: Myelination occurred more frequently along uninterrupted interbranch segments greater than 17.4 µm (AUC = 0.79; sensitivity = 97.2%, specificity = 60.4%).
source: We found that myelination occurred more frequently along uninterrupted interbranch segments greater than 17.4 µm (AUC = 0.79; sensitivity = 97.2%, specificity = 60.4%; Figure 2f,g).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: 48% of interbranch segments >17.4 µm were unmyelinated (35 of 73 segments).
source: However, similar to the relationship with axonal diameter, a substantial proportion of interbranch segments >17.4 µm were unmyelinated (48%, 35 of 73 segments).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: Using a bivariate ROC analysis, the optimal interbranch distance and axonal diameter were 13.7 µm and 334 nm, respectively (AUC = 0.99).
source: Using a bivariate ROC analysis, the optimal interbranch distance and axonal diameter were 13.7 µm and 334 nm, respectively (AUC = 0.99; Figure 2f,g).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The joint combination of interbranch distance (13.7 µm) and axonal diameter (334 nm) correctly predicted whether 128 of 132 segments contained an internode (97.0% accuracy).
source: The joint combination of these two thresholds correctly predicted whether 128 of 132 segments contained an internode (97.0% accuracy), a significant improvement over the univariate models (interbranch distance: 70.5% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p<0.001; axonal diameter: 87.9% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p=0.005).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The bivariate model was a significant improvement over the univariate interbranch distance model (70.5% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p<0.001).
source: The joint combination of these two thresholds correctly predicted whether 128 of 132 segments contained an internode (97.0% accuracy), a significant improvement over the univariate models (interbranch distance: 70.5% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p<0.001; axonal diameter: 87.9% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p=0.005).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The bivariate model was a significant improvement over the univariate axonal diameter model (87.9% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p=0.005).
source: The joint combination of these two thresholds correctly predicted whether 128 of 132 segments contained an internode (97.0% accuracy), a significant improvement over the univariate models (interbranch distance: 70.5% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p<0.001; axonal diameter: 87.9% accuracy, Fisher's Exact Test p=0.005).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The bivariate model correctly predicted 35 of 36 myelinated internodes (sensitivity = 97.2%).
source: In particular, the bivariate model correctly predicted 35 of 36 myelinated internodes (sensitivity = 97.2%), matching that of the univariate predictors (Fisher's Exact Test p=0.99).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The joint combination of interbranch distance and axonal diameter predicted with high accuracy those segments in which myelination was absent (93 of 96 segments, specificity = 96.9%).
source: However, the joint combination of interbranch distance and axonal diameter also predicted with high accuracy those segments in which myelination was absent (93 of 96 segments, specificity = 96.9%), in contrast to the univariate models (Fisher's Exact Test; axonal diameter: p=0.004, interbranch distance: p<0.001).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: Nearly all of the virally labeled cells were immunopositive for PV (93.9 ± 1.3%).
source: We also confirmed that nearly all of the virally labeled cells were immunopositive for PV (93.9 ± 1.3%; Figure 3b–d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Myelination was observed exclusively around PV+ axonal fibers with shaft diameters > 330 nm.
source: Consistent with the fluorescence microscopy analysis (Figure 2), myelination was observed exclusively around PV+ axonal fibers with shaft diameters > 330 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on electron microscopy data.

claim: Mean diameter of myelinated PV+ axonal segments was significantly larger than unmyelinated segments (Figure 3g).
source: Mean diameter was significantly larger in myelinated than in unmyelinated segments (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3g.

claim: Deletion of the Tsc1 gene induces enlarged somata of various neuronal cell types across a diversity of brain regions.
source: Deletion of the Tsc1 gene has been previously shown to induce enlarged somata of various neuronal cell types across a diversity of brain regions (Fu et al., 2012; Normand et al., 2013; Meikle et al., 2007; Carson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: The Akt-mTOR pathway is one of the main regulators of axon caliber.
source: Moreover, the Akt-mTOR pathway, a downstream target of Tsc1, is one of the main regulators of axon caliber (Markus et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation to prior work.

claim: Mice harboring a deletion of Ube3a exhibit smaller neurons with reduced axonal diameters in corpus callosum.
source: Conversely, mice harboring a deletion of Ube3a have recently been shown to exhibit smaller neurons (Sidorov et al., 2018; Wallace et al., 2012) with reduced axonal diameters in corpus callosum (Judson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations to prior work.

claim: PV+ cells in adult mPFC of PV::TSC1 mice exhibited a ~50% increase in soma size.
source: PV+ cells in adult mPFC of PV::TSC1 mice exhibited a ~50% increase in soma size, in accordance with a strong upregulation of pS6235/236, a downstream target of mTOR (Figure 4b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: PV::TSC1 cells showed a strong upregulation of pS6235/236, a downstream target of mTOR.
source: PV+ cells in adult mPFC of PV::TSC1 mice exhibited a ~50% increase in soma size, in accordance with a strong upregulation of pS6235/236, a downstream target of mTOR (Figure 4b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: PV::TSC1 cells showed filopodia-like extensions on their soma and proximal dendrite, which were not observed in PV::WT cells.
source: PV::TSC1 cells showed filopodia-like extensions on their soma and proximal dendrite, which were not observed in PV::WT cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1f.

claim: PV::UBE3A mice exhibited a ~15% reduction in PV+ interneuron soma area.
source: Conversely, PV::UBE3A mice exhibited a ~15% reduction in PV+ interneuron soma area (Figure 4b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: mPFC PV cell density was similar across PV::UBE3A, PV::TSC1, and PV::WT mice.
source: Notably, mPFC PV cell density was similar across PV::UBE3A, PV::TSC1, and PV::WT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 3a–b).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: PV::TSC1 PV+ cells showed a significantly increased primary axonal caliber compared to PV::WT cells.
source: Consistent with enlarged somata, this analysis revealed a significantly increased primary axonal caliber of PV::TSC1 PV+ cells compared to PV::WT cells (Figure 4e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Axons from PV::UBE3A showed a non-significant trend toward decreased primary axon caliber compared to PV::WT cells.
source: In contrast, axons from PV::UBE3A showed a non-significant trend toward decreased primary axon caliber compared to PV::WT cells (Figure 4e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Recorded PV+ cells in PV::TSC1, PV::UBE3A and PV::WT exhibited fast-spiking firing characteristics, with no detectable differences between genotypes.
source: Recorded PV+ cells in PV::TSC1, PV::UBE3A and PV::WT exhibited fast-spiking firing characteristics, with no detectable differences between genotypes (Figure 5b–d; Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5 and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: All PV::TSC1 cells exhibited axonal myelination (13 of 13 cells; 100%).
source: Confocal imaging followed by proximal axonal reconstructions (Figure 5e–h) revealed that all PV::TSC1 cells exhibited axonal myelination (13 of 13 cells; 100%; Figure 5f–i), similar to PV::WT cells (10 of 11 cells; 90%) and PV::UBE3A cells (7 of 8 cells; 88%).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5.

claim: PV::WT cells exhibited axonal myelination (10 of 11 cells; 90%).
source: Confocal imaging followed by proximal axonal reconstructions (Figure 5e–h) revealed that all PV::TSC1 cells exhibited axonal myelination (13 of 13 cells; 100%; Figure 5f–i), similar to PV::WT cells (10 of 11 cells; 90%) and PV::UBE3A cells (7 of 8 cells; 88%).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5.

claim: PV::UBE3A cells exhibited axonal myelination (7 of 8 cells; 88%).
source: Confocal imaging followed by proximal axonal reconstructions (Figure 5e–h) revealed that all PV::TSC1 cells exhibited axonal myelination (13 of 13 cells; 100%; Figure 5f–i), similar to PV::WT cells (10 of 11 cells; 90%) and PV::UBE3A cells (7 of 8 cells; 88%).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Tsc1-deficient PV+ cells showed increased axonal myelination per cell compared to PV::WT cells.
source: Tsc1-deficient PV+ cells showed increased axonal myelination per cell compared to PV::WT cells (Figure 5j).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5j.

claim: The increase in myelination per cell in PV::TSC1 was associated with both an increase of average internode length and a higher number of internodes per cell.
source: Interestingly, the increase in myelination per cell was associated with both an increase of average internode length (Figure 5k) as well as a higher number of internodes per cell (Figure 5l), but without a change of interbranch distance (Figure 5m).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5.

claim: PV::TSC1 cells showed no change in interbranch distance compared to controls.
source: Interestingly, the increase in myelination per cell was associated with both an increase of average internode length (Figure 5k) as well as a higher number of internodes per cell (Figure 5l), but without a change of interbranch distance (Figure 5m).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5m.

claim: Onset of myelination was unchanged in PV::TSC1 cells.

claim: Ube3a-deficient PV+ cells exhibited a decrease in axonal myelination.
source: In contrast to PV::TSC1 cells, Ube3a-deficient PV+ cells exhibited a decrease in axonal myelination (Figure 5i,j), including both a lower number and shorter length of internodes (Figure 5k,l), consistent with their reduced soma size.

claim: Ube3a-deficient PV+ cells showed both a lower number and shorter length of internodes.
source: In contrast to PV::TSC1 cells, Ube3a-deficient PV+ cells exhibited a decrease in axonal myelination (Figure 5i,j), including both a lower number and shorter length of internodes (Figure 5k,l), consistent with their reduced soma size.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The initial point of myelin onset from the soma was unchanged in PV::UBE3A cells.
source: Finally, the initial point of myelin onset from the soma was unchanged in PV::UBE3A cells (Figure 5n).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5n.

claim: No robust changes were observed in global myelination in PV::TSC1 or PV::UBE3A mice.
source: Despite these PV+ cell type-specific alterations in myelination, no robust changes were observed in global myelination (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a,b) or CC1+ mature oligodendrocyte density (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: No robust changes were observed in CC1+ mature oligodendrocyte density in PV::TSC1 or PV::UBE3A mice.
source: Despite these PV+ cell type-specific alterations in myelination, no robust changes were observed in global myelination (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a,b) or CC1+ mature oligodendrocyte density (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: ROC analysis of PV::UBE3A cells yielded bivariate thresholds of axonal diameter >332 nm and interbranch distance >14.1 µm (sensitivity = 100%, specificity = 97.5%; AUC = 0.99).
source: ROC analysis of PV::UBE3A cells yielded bivariate thresholds of axonal diameter >332 nm and interbranch distance >14.1 µm (sensitivity = 100%, specificity = 97.5%; AUC = 0.99) (Figure 5p,q).

claim: ROC analysis of PV::TSC1 cells yielded bivariate thresholds of axonal diameter >378 nm and interbranch distance >18.6 µm (sensitivity = 100%, specificity = 94.6%; AUC = 0.99).

claim: For PV::UBE3A, the bivariate model was a significant improvement over the univariate model based on interbranch distance (p=0.004).

claim: For PV::UBE3A, the bivariate model was statistically similar to the univariate model for axonal diameter (p=0.500).
source: For PV::UBE3A, the bivariate model was a significant improvement over the univariate model based on interbranch distance (p=0.004), but statistically similar to the univariate model for axonal diameter (p=0.500).

claim: SOM+ interneurons contribute minimally to total neocortical myelination content.
